_comment: Python (pip-audit) vulnerability findings this repo has deliberately decided NOT to fix by upgrading, with the reason recorded here rather than only in a workflow comment. Read by .github/workflows/test.yml's pip-audit step, which turns each "python" entry into a --ignore-vuln flag, and by scripts/npm_audit_gate.py for the "npm" list (npm audit has no --ignore flag, so the filtering is done on the parsed JSON instead). This file exists because test.yml and frontend-tests.yml's own header comments already referenced it as the established escape hatch ('record why it is unreachable in .github/audit-allowlist.json') before it was ever actually built -- CLAUDE.md's own standing rule is to carry a stated decision through to the code that enforces it, not just describe it. Every entry needs an id, package, fix_version (from pip-audit's own output), reason, and added date. A red pip-audit gate for anything NOT listed here still means upgrade the pin -- this file is for genuinely irreconcilable constraints, never a shortcut around one that could just be fixed.

python.reason: Temporary compatibility exception: setuptools<84 preserves pkg_resources required by webrtcvad through resemblyzer and voice authentication. This advisory requires Windows plus attacker-controlled namespace metadata passed to setuptools.wheel.Wheel.install_as_egg. The deployed Linux API is not affected by that Windows path interpretation, application code does not call this legacy installer, and installs use trusted hash-locked requirements rather than user-provided wheels. Do not broaden this exception to other setuptools advisories. Retire it when webrtcvad/resemblyzer no longer requires pkg_resources and setuptools>=84.1.0 can pass voice-authentication tests.

npm.reason: There is no version of picomatch that fixes this. The advisory range is <=4.0.7 and 4.0.7 IS the latest published release (npm dist-tag latest, checked 2026-11-17), so no lockfile change can clear it; npm's own suggested remedy, a major vitest upgrade, would not either, since vitest still depends on picomatch. The advisory is a regular-expression denial of service triggered by a glob pattern with a single-branch repeated extglob. picomatch reaches this repo only at BUILD, TEST and DEV time, in all three Node projects (homeschool-tutor, demo, license-server): through vite, vitest and tinyglobby/fdir, and through tailwindcss's content globbing and chokidar's file watching (via micromatch, anymatch, readdirp). Every copy is marked dev in the lockfiles; it is in no shipped browser bundle and not in the license-server Worker, so no visitor, child, parent or customer can reach it. The patterns it compiles are the ones written in our own build and test configuration; supplying a malicious one requires editing this repository's configuration, at which point the glob matcher is not the problem. Same shape as the braces entry above. Revisit when picomatch publishes a fix, which makes this a lockfile refresh plus deleting this entry.
